battle.name: 積石軍之戰
battle.brief: 天寶六載（747）七月，吐蕃攻陷鄯、廓二州，涼州戒嚴。河西節度使哥舒翰率蕃、漢兵自河源出師，轉戰積石山，攻破洪濟城，斬獲甚眾；旋奏置河源軍、積石軍於鄯州境，扼住積石關。本卡羅馬短劍未出土於此役，只以短刺佩兵的戰術位階，對照唐軍直刃佩刀與吐蕃環首短刀。

kit.name: 羅馬短劍
kit.history: 刺劍不是用來揮砍的。短兵相接靠的是盾的邊緣和刺突的節奏。

countries: 積石軍之戰是天寶六載（747）唐朝與吐蕃在青海河湟地區的一場邊境戰事，交戰方分為唐軍與吐蕃軍兩個系統。唐軍方面，戰區最高統帥是河西節度使，節度使駐節涼州，轄涼、甘、肅、瓜、沙等河西諸州以及鄯、廓二州；作戰編制以折衝兵制為骨架，一軍約二千人，兵序列上另設河源軍、積石軍等名號，兵源以募兵制的邊軍為主，並徵用吐谷渾、突騎施一系的蕃部騎兵，以及自長安、洛陽調發的蕃漢混編部隊，兵種分為騎兵、步兵、弓弩手與專司強攻的攻城隊。唐軍的長處是騎射與攻守器械，短處是青海高原的距離與糧秣。吐蕃方面，由贊普墀都東贊（赤松德贊）統治下的河湟方面軍經辦，部隊以高原蕃兵為主，輔以被征服的羌、吐谷渾部眾，騎兵比例高、紀律嚴、熟悉隘道，作戰以築城據險、斷絕糧道、襲擾驛傳為主要手段。地理上，積石山扼住黃河上游，東連鄯、廓，西望河西走廊；誰佔據積石山，誰就掌握青海與河西之間的通道。因此這場爭奪並非單一城池的攻防，而是整條邊境補給線的掌握。
countriesEn: The Battle of Jishi Army was a frontier war fought in the Huangshui region of Qinghai in 747, during the sixth year of the Tianbao era, between the Tang dynasty and the Tibetan empire, and it divided into two systems: the Tang army and the Tibetan army. On the Tang side, the supreme commander of the theatre was the jiedushi of Hexi, whose headquarters sat at Liangzhou and whose authority covered the Hexi prefectures of Liang, Gan, Su, Gua and Sha as well as the two prefectures of Shan and Guo. The order of battle rested on the fubing skeleton, with about two thousand men to a regiment, and additional designations such as the Heyuan Army and the Jishi Army. Manpower was mainly recruited frontier troops, supplemented by tribal horsemen from the Tuyuhun and the Qikishi branches and by mixed Han-Tibetan units dispatched from Chang'an and Luoyang. Arms were divided into cavalry, infantry, crossbowmen and specialist assault teams. Tang strength lay in mounted archery and siege equipment; its weakness was distance and supply in the high plateau. On the Tibetan side, the operation was run by the fronts command of the Tibetan empire under the tsanpo Trisong Detsen, with a core of plateau tribal troops reinforced by conquered Qiang and Tuyuhun elements, a high proportion of cavalry, strict discipline and close familiarity with the defiles; its method was to build fortified posts on the ridges, cut supply lines and raid the relay stations. Geographically Jishi Mountain commands the upper Yellow River, linking Shan and Guo in the east to the Hexi corridor in the west. Whoever held Jishi Mountain held the corridor between Qinghai and Hexi, so the contest was not for a single town but for control of the whole frontier line of supply.
people: 唐軍主帥哥舒翰是這場戰役的關鍵人物。他是突騎施西突厥別部哥舒部人，父哥舒道元歷任安西都護將軍、赤水軍使，家世以武勇著稱；哥舒翰自隴右節度使王忠嗣幕府起家，能讀《左氏春秋》《漢書》，頗得士卒擁戴。天寶六載，他以大斗軍副使、隴右節度副使、關西兵馬使、河源軍使的身份受命主軍，其後升任河西節度使，總攬河西戰區。至於副手與部將，《舊唐書》《新唐書》本傳多略去姓名，只留下「蕃漢兵」「先鋒」「遊騎」一類的稱呼，無法確定具體統兵者；較可依據的只有《舊唐書》記其於天寶年間與吐蕃戰於苦拔海、屢破之。前任河西節度使王忠嗣是本戰役的另一位重要人物：他主張持守，反對在糧秣不繼、士卒疲敝的條件下深入吐蕃要地，因而被宰相李林甫以「欲奉太子」為由讒陷，貶為漢陽太守；玄宗改用哥舒翰主戰，正是要打破這種守勢。李林甫是朝廷層面的推手，他以文制武、頻換邊將，把邊防的成敗繫於人事。吐蕃方面的決策者是贊普墀都東贊，其時吐蕃正把佛苯兩套傳統與新佔領區編入帝國，兵力和糧秣可自青海腹地調集，惟前線將領姓名諸說並存，本卡不強行指定。兩年後（天寶八載，749）攻石堡城時，哥舒翰曾限先鋒官高秀岩、張守瑜三日付命，可見這套指揮作風延續至此。
peopleEn: The key figure on the Tang side was Geshu Han, the commander of the Tang army. He was a member of the Geshu tribe of the Qikishi, a branch of the Western Turks, and his father Geshu Daoyuan had served as Protector General of Anxi and commander of the Chishui Army, so the family was already known for arms. Geshu Han began inside the staff of the Longyou jiedushi Wang Zhongsi, could read the Chunqiu Commentary of Zuo and the Hanshu, and was trusted by the soldiers. In 747 he was entrusted with command as deputy of the Dadou Army, deputy jiedushi of Longyou, commissioner of troops for the passes of Guan, and commander of the Heyuan Army; he was later promoted to jiedushi of Hexi and took overall command of the theatre. As for his subordinates and divisional commanders, the Old and New Tang histories mostly omit names and leave only collective labels such as the Han and tribal troops, the vanguard or the mounted scouts, so the individuals in command cannot be fixed. The better-attested line is the Old Tang History notice that he fought the Tibetans at Kubaihai during the Tianbao years and defeated them repeatedly. The former Hexi jiedushi Wang Zhongsi was the other important man: he argued for holding position and refused to strike deep into Tibetan territory while supply was short and the troops exhausted, and was therefore denounced by the chancellor Li Linfu on the charge of intending to enthrone the crown prince, and demoted to governor of Hanyang. When Xuanzong replaced him with Geshu Han, the point was precisely to break that defensive mood. Li Linfu was the hand behind the decision at court level, preferring civil officials to military ones, rotating frontier commanders constantly and tying the quality of the frontier defence to personal appointments. On the Tibetan side the decision-maker was the tsanpo Trisong Detsen, under whom the empire was folding its Buddhist and Bon traditions and its new conquests into a single polity, so that troops and grain could be drawn from the interior of Qinghai; the names of the commanders in the front line vary from source to source and this card does not force a single identification. Two years later, in 749, when Geshu Han attacked Shibao fortress, he gave his vanguard officers Gao Xiuyan and Zhang Shoyu three days to take it, which shows that this command style carried on.
kits: 本卡所配兵器是羅馬短劍（Gladius），公元前1世紀的羅馬軍用短刺佩兵：劍身狹長而直，握柄在臨戰時可以雙手穩定握持，護手兼作破壞與敲擊的部位，重心靠近劍尖，設計重點是刺而非劈砍，配合方盾的盾緣使用，講究的是「刺的節奏」而不是揮砍的力道——這正是卡面「短兵相接靠的是盾的邊緣和刺突的節奏」的由來。必須說明的是：747年的積石山戰場上沒有羅馬短劍，漢文史料所記此役唐軍的刀兵是直刃的橫刀、儀刀一類佩刀，吐蕃戰士則用環首短刀一類佩兵，考古發掘的吐蕃時期墓葬中亦見環首刀與鐵鏃、馬具等實物。因此這件兵器在戰役中的位置是「對照」而非「實裝」：它標示的是短兵相接最後一環的戰術位階——在城頭窄地、壕塹與屍體之間，短刺型佩刀與盾、矛、長刀構成的組合，才是攻守雙方真正決定勝負的地方。唐軍在積石山一役可考的器械另有其物：鎧甲有明光甲與黑甲一類的札甲，弓弩有步弓、角弓與擘張一類的強弩，攻城則靠具車、雲梯、撞竿與火箭、投石一類的器械配合；高原柴薪極乏，軍中以牛糞曬乾充作燃料，這是青海作戰與內地不同的實情。運輸以牛、驢騾為主，糧秣靠青稞、芻粟與軍屯，沿黃河渡口有舟與皮囊過河，馬匹是關鍵的戰略物資，攻下牧區、奪取馬群往往比奪下一座城更能改變戰局。
kitsEn: The weapon on this card is the Roman gladius, a short stabbing sidearm of the first century BC: a narrow, straight blade, a grip that could be steadied with both hands in close fighting, a guard that doubled as a striking and breaking point, and a weight set forward near the tip, so that the design favours the thrust rather than the cut, used together with the edge of a rectangular shield, and it is the rhythm of the stab rather than the force of the swing that counts. This is the origin of the line on the card face, that close combat depends on the edge of the shield and the rhythm of the thrust. It must be said plainly that there was no gladius on the field of Jishi Mountain in 747: the Chinese sources recording this campaign describe the Tang blades as straight-edged pendants of the hengdao and yidao type, while Tibetan fighters used short ring-pommel knives, and excavated Tibetan-period burials have yielded ring-pommel knives along with iron arrowheads and harness fittings. The position of this weapon in the campaign is therefore a comparison, not an actual issue: it marks the tactical station of the last link in close fighting. Between the parapet, the ditch and the dead, the combination of a short stabbing blade with shield, spear and long sword is what actually decides the outcome for both sides. The other equipment of the Tang army at Jishi is more firmly attested: lamellar armour of the Mingguang and black-armour types, bows and crossbows including step bows, horn bows and strong siege-type tension bows, and for the assault the trebuchet-style wheeled frames, scaling ladders, battering poles and fire and stone-throwing devices working together. Fuel was acutely scarce on the plateau, and dried cow dung was burned in camp, a practical difference between operations in Qinghai and in the interior. Transport rested on oxen, donkeys and mules; the food supply on barley, fodder millet and garrison farms; crossing the Yellow River used boats and skin rafts at the fords. Horses were the decisive strategic material, and taking pastures and herds of horses often changed the situation more than taking a walled town.
tactics: 積石山之戰的戰術過程可以分成三段。第一段是吐蕃的先手：吐蕃軍在攻取鄯州、廓州之後，沿山脊築城置塞，把唐的涼州與河西走廊逼到數日可達的距離之內，遊騎不斷切斷唐軍的糧道與傳驛，邊地的市易與驛傳因而時通時絕。第二段是唐軍的攻勢：哥舒翰以蕃、漢兵自河源一帶出發，先以騎兵掃清外圍、封住各條山道，再把步兵與攻城隊投入洪濟城的正面；攻擊時以步弓與弩手在前列成遮蔽射界，雲梯、具車、撞竿同時靠城，城頭的燃火與投石使唐軍攻具屢屢受損，而攻破之後在突破口內短兵相接，正是短刺型佩刀、盾與長刀組成的近戰組合最吃重的場合。第三段是追擊與設防：破城之後，唐軍在狹窄山道上追擊潰退的吐蕃騎兵，吐蕃以弓石與隘口阻滯追兵，雙方在積石山南北反覆拉鋸。戰後的部署同樣屬於戰術的一部分：唐廷依此形勝，在鄯州境內置河源軍與積石軍，積石軍扼積石關，壘堡、置烽燧、屯芻穀，以騎巡警戒河曲，讓吐蕃無法再順利南出。整體而言，唐軍靠騎兵機動、器械攻堅與前進堡寨三件事，彌補了青海作戰的距離劣勢；吐蕃則靠據險、斷糧與馬力周旋，把唐軍的攻勢消耗在隘口之前。
tacticsEn: The tactical course of the battle at Jishi Mountain can be divided into three phases. The first was the Tibetan initiative: after taking Shan and Guo prefectures, the Tibetan army built forts and barricades along the ridges, pushing the Tang positions at Liangzhou and the Hexi corridor to within a few days' march, while their mounted scouts kept cutting Tang supply lines and relay communications, so that frontier markets and the postal service worked only intermittently. The second was the Tang offensive: Geshu Han marched out with Han and tribal troops from the Heyuan area, first clearing the outskirts with cavalry and sealing the various mountain tracks, then committing infantry and assault teams against the front of Hongji city. During the attack, step bows and crossbowmen formed a screen of overlapping fire in front, while scaling ladders, wheeled frames and battering poles were brought up to the wall at the same time; fire-throwing and stone-throwing from the parapet repeatedly damaged the Tang assault equipment, and once the breach was opened, the close-quarter struggle inside it was precisely the moment when the short stabbing blade, the shield and the long sword carried the heaviest weight. The third phase was pursuit and fortification: after the city fell, the Tang pursued the routed Tibetan cavalry along narrow tracks, and the Tibetans checked the pursuit with arrows, stones and defiles, the two sides locking and unlocking along the length of Jishi Mountain. The post-battle deployment was itself part of the tactics: on the strength of that terrain the Tang court set up the Heyuan Army and the Jishi Army within Shan prefecture, the Jishi Army holding Jishi Pass with stacked stockades, beacon towers and stored fodder, patrolling the bends of the river with mounted men so that the Tibetans could no longer move south easily. Taken as a whole, the Tang compensated for the handicap of distance in operations in Qinghai through cavalry mobility, siege engineering and forward stockades; the Tibetans, relying on holding the heights, cutting supply and the stamina of their horses, wore out the Tang offensive before the defiles.
data: 關於這一戰，漢文史料留下的數字並不多。以下只列可以核對或有明確依據的項目，並標明哪些屬於推算。第一，時間：天寶六載即公元747年，戰役及朝廷往返議事的過程集中在該年夏季，《舊唐書》《資治通鑑》多繫於七月前後，具體日數各書不一。第二，地點與距離：積石山在黃河上游北岸，積石關一帶在今青海積石山、黃南一帶，與唐代鄯州治所（今青海樂都）相距數十里至百餘里，各家考證略有出入；由涼州出發的後勤線長達數百里，沿途需設驛站、屯田與烽燧接力。第三，兵力：唐軍自河源、鄯州方向出動，舊、新唐書僅概稱「蕃、漢兵」，未給確數；若按唐代一軍約二千人的編制推算，數萬之師約相當十餘軍，但這是編制推算而非史載確數；吐蕃一方的投入同樣只有概數，諸書多以「眾」「蕃兵數萬」一類的模糊語句帶過。第四，戰果：傳記有斬首數千、俘獲甚眾之類的說法，確數無從核實，可確認的只有一點，即吐蕃在洪濟一線的堡寨被唐軍攻破，其對黃河上游的控制力一度中斷。第五，後續代價：兩年後（749）哥舒翰攻石堡城，攻城過程中唐軍士卒死傷極重，《舊唐書》《資治通鑑》有「死者數萬」之語，具體數目各家考證不一，卻足以說明強攻的殘酷。第六，後勤：青海高海拔地帶燃料極乏，軍隊以牛糞曬乾與灌木柴為主要燃料，糧秣依賴河湟的青稞與芻穀，馬匹多取自被奪取的牧區，這是每次出兵都要先解決的問題。
dataEn: The Chinese sources preserve few figures for this campaign, so only the items that can be checked or that rest on a clear basis are listed here, with the calculated ones marked as such. First, the date: the sixth year of Tianbao, that is 747 CE, with the fighting and the exchange of memorials at court falling in the summer of that year; the Old Tang History and the Comprehensive Mirror place it around the seventh month, though the exact day differs from source to source. Second, place and distance: Jishi Mountain stands on the north bank of the upper Yellow River, the area of Jishi Pass corresponding broadly to present-day Jishishan and Huangnan in Qinghai, some tens of li to a little over a hundred li from the seat of Tang-era Shan prefecture at modern Ledu; the scholarly estimates differ slightly. The logistics line running back to Liangzhou was several hundred li long and required relay stations, garrison farms and beacon towers strung out along it. Third, strength: the Tang army moved out from the Heyuan and Shan side, and the Old and New Tang histories give only the general description of Han and tribal troops, with no exact figure; calculated at the Tang rate of about two thousand men to a regiment, a force of several thousand would amount to a dozen or more regiments, but that is arithmetic on the establishment, not a recorded number. The Tibetan commitment is equally given only in general terms, the books using vague phrases such as a multitude of them or several tens of thousands of tribal troops. Fourth, results: the records speak of several thousand heads taken and much captured, none of which can be verified; what can be confirmed is that the Tibetan forts on the Hongji line were stormed by the Tang and that Tibetan control of the upper Yellow River was interrupted for a time. Fifth, the later cost: two years afterwards, in 749, when Geshu Han attacked Shibao fortress, Tang soldiers died in great numbers during the assault, the Old Tang History and the Comprehensive Mirror both speaking of tens of thousands of dead, though the exact figure is disputed; it is enough to show how brutal the storming was. Sixth, logistics: fuel was acutely scarce on the high plateau, and the army burned dried cow dung and gathered scrub wood, subsisting on barley and fodder millet from the Huangshui valley, while horses were taken mostly from captured pastures.
cause: 積石軍之戰的起因可以分成遠因與近因兩層。遠因是青藏高原上的吐蕃帝國在七世紀中葉完成對青海湖一帶的整合，取得河湟與河西東端的門戶，取得地盤即取得進攻跳板；此時唐朝的西北邊防正處在制度轉折點，府兵制崩解、募兵邊軍成為主力，邊鎮權力集中於節度使之手，而朝廷以宰相李林甫為首的用人方式強調以文制武、避免邊將久握重兵，結果是人人願意守土、無人肯於深入，邊防整體轉為被動。近因是吐蕃在西北的連續攻勢：天寶五載、六載之交，吐蕃大軍壓向河湟，鄯州、廓州相繼失守，涼州戒嚴，河西走廊這條唐廷賴以運轉的絲路與糧道受到直接威脅，長安的朝廷不能接受邊境被切開的局面。直接導火線是人事：河西節度使王忠嗣反對在後援不繼的情況下深入，被李林甫以「欲奉太子」的罪名貶黜，玄宗隨即起用敢於用兵的哥舒翰，河西方面於是轉入主動出擊。一場新的攻勢在748年之前的幾個月裡被定下來：先取積石山、洪濟一線的據點，再以堡寨長期控制河湟的門戶，把邊防從「守住」改為「向前推出去」。至於戰爭是否更早源於宗教、婚姻或貿易上的衝突，漢文與藏文記載都沒有足夠清晰的因果鏈，本卡不強行推斷。
causeEn: The causes of the Battle of Jishi Army divide into a distant layer and a proximate one. The distant cause is that the Tibetan empire on the Tibetan plateau had, by the middle of the seventh century, completed its integration of the area around Qinghai Lake and gained the door to the eastern end of the Hexi corridor; territory was the platform for attack. At the same time the Tang northwest frontier stood at an institutional turning point, with the fubing system collapsing, recruited frontier troops becoming the main force, and military authority concentrating in the hands of the jiedushi, while the court's way of appointing under Chancellor Li Linfu preferred civil officers to soldiers and avoided letting frontier commanders hold great power for long. The result was that everyone was willing to hold his own ground and no one would strike deep, and the frontier turned passive. The proximate cause was the series of Tibetan offensives in the northwest: around the fifth and sixth years of Tianbao the Tibetan main force pressed towards Huangshui, Shan and Guo prefectures fell one after another, Liangzhou was put on alert, and the Hexi corridor, that artery of silk-road traffic and grain transport on which the Tang court depended, was directly threatened; the court at Chang'an could not accept having the frontier cut in two. The immediate trigger was a personnel decision: Wang Zhongsi, jiedushi of Hexi, opposed going deep without follow-up support and was demoted by Li Linfu on the charge of intending to enthrone the crown prince, and Xuanzong promptly put the bellicose Geshu Han in command, so that the Hexi front shifted to the offensive. A new offensive was settled in the months before 748: take the strongpoints on the Jishi Mountain and Hongji line first, then hold the door to Huangshui with forts and stockades for the long term, converting the frontier from holding to pushing forward. As for whether the war stemmed from still earlier conflicts of religion, marriage or trade, neither the Chinese nor the Tibetan records supply a clear enough chain of causation, and this card does not force one.
impact: 這場戰役的直接影響，是唐朝第一次在河湟方向把防禦線推出去並且站住腳跟。積石山、洪濟與其後取下的石堡城，構成一組彼此策應的堡寨節點，夾在河湟與河西之間；同時設立的河源軍與積石軍，把節度使體制下的兵制、糧秣與屯田第一次成建制地放到青海高原上，而不再是短期的奔襲掠地。這條補給線一旦成立，749年哥舒翰才能以石堡城為目標，於是才有天寶八載那場以傷亡換城池的強攻。制度層面的後果更為深遠：邊軍久駐、節度使兼理軍政、朝廷更換邊將成常例，安史之亂前唐廷的西北防線其實已被自己的體制掏空；755年亂起之後，吐蕃乘亂大舉東下，河西的涼、甘、肅、瓜、沙等州相繼陷落，走廊中斷數十年，直至宋代才逐步收回。西域方面，西域的交通與絲路在唐蕃兩強夾縫中維持數十年，與這條青海邊線的穩定與否直接相關。兵器與戰術層面也有沉澱：高原條件下「騎兵機動加器械攻堅加前進堡寨」的組合，被後來的唐蕃邊防沿用；而唐軍的教訓則是攻城死傷過重，說明只靠強攻難以在這種邊界上取得永久成果。史載有限，能夠確定的是：這場戰役把唐蕃在河湟的角力拉回到長期拉鋸的狀態，兩年之後的得與失都由這個起點延伸而出。
impactEn: The direct effect of this campaign was that the Tang pushed a defensive line out towards the Huangshui valley for the first time and held it. Jishi Mountain, Hongji and the Shibao fortress taken afterwards formed a set of mutually supporting fortified nodes set between Huangshui and Hexi; the Heyuan Army and the Jishi Army established at the same time put the recruiting system, the supply arrangements and the garrison farms of the jiedushi system into Qinghai on an organised scale for the first time, instead of the short rushes and raids of earlier years. Once that line of supply stood, Geshu Han could take Shibao fortress as his objective in 749, and with it came the storming of Tianbao year eight that bought a walled town at the price of severe casualties. The institutional consequences ran deeper still: troops garrisoned for long periods, jiedushi holding civil as well as military authority, and the court rotating frontier commanders as a matter of routine had hollowed out the Tang northwest frontier before the rebellion of 755. When that rebellion broke, the Tibetans came east in force, the prefecture seats of Liang, Gan, Su, Gua and Sha in Hexi fell in turn, and the corridor was cut for several decades before the Song recovered it piece by piece. On the western side, the traffic and silk routes of the far west survived for decades in the gap between two great powers, and their fate was tied directly to the stability of this Qinghai line. There are also deposits left at the level of arms and tactics: the combination of cavalry mobility, siege engineering and forward stockades became a standard in later Tang-Tibetan frontier work, while the Tang lesson was that the cost of storming was too heavy, showing that nothing durable could be gained on such a frontier by assault alone. The record is thin, but this much is certain: the campaign returned the Tang-Tibetan contest in the Huangshui valley to a long grind, and the gains and losses of the two following years both grew out of this starting point.
result: 積石軍之戰的結果，是唐軍在積石山一線取得局部主動權：洪濟城等堡寨被攻破，吐蕃在黃河上游的推進一度受挫，唐廷隨即在鄯州境內置河源軍與積石軍，把積石關變成常設的邊防節點；兩年後石堡城也被攻下，河西的門戶一度握在唐手。但這不是決定性的勝利。吐蕃並未就此退讓，天寶年間雙方在鄯、廓一線仍反覆攻守，邊境進入長期拉鋸；史書的記載在這一點上並不統一：有的只記唐軍的一次勝利，有的把此役與其後的失地並列，因此更穩妥的說法是，積石軍之戰為唐朝在青海邊防爭取到一段可守的推進線，而不是終結了唐蕃在河湟的爭端。戰役本身的細節仍然相當模糊：兵力配置、攻城序列乃至具體的月份，各書互有出入，本卡的數字一律採保守表述。卡面那件羅馬短劍並不出現在任何一支作戰序列裡，它留在卡上，是作為短刺佩兵這個戰術位階的標記：真正決定積石山攻防的，是城頭狹窄地帶上盾、短刀與長刀之間的節奏，而不是任何一件具體的兵器。
resultEn: The outcome of the Battle of Jishi Army was a local gain in initiative for the Tang on the Jishi Mountain line: forts such as Hongji city were stormed, the Tibetan advance on the upper Yellow River was checked for a time, and the court promptly set up the Heyuan Army and the Jishi Army within Shan prefecture, turning Jishi Pass into a permanent node of the frontier. Two years later Shibao fortress also fell, and for a while the door to Hexi was in Tang hands. But this was not a decisive victory. The Tibetans did not give way; through the Tianbao years the two sides continued to attack and defend each other along the Shan and Guo line, and the frontier settled into a long grind. The sources are not consistent on this point: some record only the Tang success, others set the campaign alongside the later losses of territory. The safer formulation is therefore that the battle won the Tang a defensible forward line in the Qinghai frontier rather than ending the Tang-Tibetan contest in the Huangshui valley. The details of the fighting itself remain fairly vague: the disposition of troops, the sequence of the assault and even the month are reported differently, and the figures on this card are all given conservatively. The Roman gladius on the card face appears in no order of battle at all. It stays on the card as a marker of the tactical station of the short stabbing sidearm: what decided the fighting at Jishi Mountain was the rhythm between shield, short knife and long sword in the narrow ground of the parapet, and not any particular weapon.
